skill.displayName: Leaf Curling & Margin Scorch Diagnosis | 植物卷叶/焦边识别（干旱/病害）

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised plant analysis, but it also silently links users to remote accounts and stores authentication tokens locally with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: Leaf curling/scorch analysis through a remote API is coherent with the stated purpose, and cloud history is described, but the implementation also includes silent account provisioning, token handling, local user persistence, and broad shared HTTP/CRUD helpers that exceed a simple diagnosis workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions visibly require automatic cloud history queries and tell the agent not to ask for or reveal identity values; this is disclosed in the artifact, but it reduces user-directed control over account-linked operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No VirusTotal signal was supplied and there is no evident install-time execution; the static scan raw-IP warning comes from an inactive dev config while the prod config uses public lifeemergence.com endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local media files for upload, accepts remote URLs, reads environment/workspace identity values including data/smyx-api-key.txt, detects workspace paths, and writes a workspace SQLite database; these are only partially disclosed and are broad for the stated task.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The local sys_user database stores user profile fields plus token/open_token values, and outbound requests attach those tokens and identifiers after silent remote login/provisioning.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with plant images/videos and account-linked report history being sent to the LifeEmergence backend, and with the skill creating or reusing a local identity database that may store tokens. Avoid using it on sensitive farm imagery or private workspace identities unless the publisher clarifies retention, token storage, and account-provisioning behavior.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic DAO filters are real but appear to be internal generic database helpers, not an exposed query interface in the leaf diagnosis CLI; this was downgraded as a supporting code-quality risk rather than the main concern.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill text discloses API use, file input, output files, and internal identity handling, but the manifest-level permissions and token/database persistence are not clearly declared.
[TP4] unexpected: The leaf-analysis wrapper is purpose-aligned, but the account creation, token recovery, and shared identity infrastructure materially expand the trust boundary beyond what a user would expect from plant diagnosis alone.
[SDI-1] expected: Cloud history listing is explicitly documented and wired through --list, so it is not hidden; it remains a review concern because it is automatic and account-linked.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Open-id resolution, workspace credential-file reading, and persistent local identity reuse are artifact-backed and only partially explained to users.
[SDI-4] expected: The generic video-analysis base module exists, but the published wrapper sets the plant diagnosis scene code and user-facing text; this supports a mismatch note, not a malicious finding.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad default and history triggers are visible in SKILL.md; they are still concerning because they can initiate remote, account-linked processing from broad natural-language phrases.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading provided files or URLs to a remote analysis API is expected for this cloud AI skill, but the code lacks an explicit runtime consent gate and combines uploads with identity headers.
[E1] unexpected: The outbound phoneLogin/provisioning request with openId/mobile/source is confirmed in util.py and is the strongest artifact-backed concern because it silently creates or recovers remote account state.
[P2] expected: The detected Unicode character is a zero-width joiner inside a visible emoji sequence, not hidden behavior-changing text; this finding was downgraded.
[YR4] expected: The metadata description is ordinary bilingual skill metadata; the same Unicode indicator does not by itself prove metadata poisoning.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The raw IP appears only in config-dev.yaml, while runtime config.yaml selects prod endpoints; it is a maintenance/provenance note rather than the basis for the verdict.
